frozen_by: Claude Code, claude-opus-5-5 (desktop app), executing PLAN.md as written; additions beyond PLAN.md are marked added_beyond_plan

metric_definitions.RPS: normalized individual-rating ranked probability score (1/5) sum_{k=0}^{4} (Q(k) - 1{y<=k})^2; range 0..1; lower is better; averaged over ratings within an artifact, then equally over artifacts
metric_definitions.CE: -ln q(y) in nats, no implicit floor; infinity is retained
metric_definitions.TVD_population: 0.5 sum_y |q(y) - p(y)| against the known synthetic distribution; range 0..1
metric_definitions.TVD_empirical: 0.5 sum_y |q(y) - p_hat(y)| against an artifact's observed expert-rating frequencies (Phase C only); a different, noisy comparison
metric_definitions.bias: judge mean minus human mean on the 0..5 scale; positive means lenient
metric_definitions.undefined: a coefficient whose denominator is zero is reported as undefined (null), never as 1

human_population.form: p_x = (9/10) Binomial(5, theta_x) + (1/10) Uniform{0..5}; strictly positive; min p_x(y) >= 1/60
human_population.object_universe: uniform over the 11 artifacts j = 1..11; population variance uses divisor 11
human_population.relation_to_experiment_01: binomial family as in 01_conditional_binomial_distribution_identification_start_08Nov2026, mixed with a uniform component so every category has positive probability; 01's frozen files are not modified

A1.epsilon: min_y p_x(y) / 6 (the largest value allowed by PLAN.md)

A1_max.reason: PLAN.md's epsilon bound guarantees positivity but makes the perturbation small; this shows the largest same-mean, same-variance RPS gap under a declared floor
A1_max.objective: maximize expected RPS excess over q with sum q = 1, mean(q) = mean(p), var(q) = var(p), q(y) >= floor; exact vertex enumeration over all 20 triples of free categories; ties keep the lexicographically first triple

A1_finite_sample.object_sampling: uniform with replacement from the 11 artifacts; the same object draw is shared by the p-panel and the q-panel within a replication; ratings drawn independently
A1_finite_sample.estimator: balanced two-way ANOVA, raw (negative estimates retained); coefficients for the mean of 3 raters computed from raw estimates

A2.wrong_forecast: for j in the subset, q_j = p_{12-j} (the mirrored low-theta distribution); elsewhere q_j = p_j
A2.constant_forecast: pbar = equal-weight average of the 11 p_x
A2.offset_population_form: h_x = (0, a/10, (10-a-c)/10, c/10, 0, 0) for (a, c) in offset_population; support {1,2,3}
A2.positive_probability_variant: g_x smoothed as (1 - 6/100) g_x + (6/100) Uniform; declared before measurement

A3.tempered_form: q_T proportional to p^(1/T); 'mode' is the point mass at argmax p (T -> 0); computed in float64
A3.sampled_histogram_rps_identity: E RPS(n-call histogram of q) = E RPS(q) + (1/5) sum_k Q(k)(1-Q(k))/n
A3.shift_family_form: p_c(y) = base(y - c + 1) on {c-1, c, c+1}

phase_b.scale: continuous Gaussian scores; no rounding or clipping; no categorical RPS/CE in this phase

evaluation.fresh: new objects from the same object distribution, new facet levels and new residuals for every design in every replication
evaluation.absolute_error: mean over objects of (object mean - universe score)^2; expectation v_Delta
evaluation.relative_error: sum over objects of (d_u - mean d)^2 / (n - 1), d_u = object mean - universe score; expectation v_delta

selectors.anova_trunc: raw ANOVA with negative estimates set to zero (secondary; labeled)

phase_b.marginal_variance_rule: sees only the single-rating marginal variance, which is identical for all designs; it cannot rank designs and is implemented as the equal design [4,4]
phase_b.formula_check_tolerance: |mean observed error - population formula| <= 3.5 Monte Carlo standard errors for each design, error type and configuration (36 checks)

V1_correlated_raters.model: rater-specific effects A, UA and AB of the second rater in each pair = rho * first + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * independent; residuals independent
V1_correlated_raters.analytic_actual: v_Delta with v_a, v_ua, v_ab multiplied by (1 + rho)

V2_group_heterogeneity.model: calibration and evaluation objects split equally between two predeclared groups with different object-by-rater interaction variance; pooled mean 0.6 equals C1

V4_dependent_occasions_in_calibration.model: in calibration only, the object-by-occasion effect is (UB)_ub = sqrt(rho) W_u + sqrt(1 - rho) Z_ub (occasions too close in time); deployment occasions are independent; the universe score excludes W

phase_b.uncertainty: Student-t 95% intervals over 256 independent replications for means and paired differences; Wilson 95% interval for proportions; p-val=n/a (no confirmatory test)

phase_c.prior_exposure: all ratings were seen in earlier work; the test split was previously used for historical evaluation; retrospective analysis only
phase_c.primary_set: historical test split: 30 artifacts, 10 tasks, all expert ratings available (2 or 3 per artifact)
phase_c.secondary_set: all 75 artifacts; train is in-sample for H1/H2 prompt development and val was used for historical selection
phase_c.human_g_study: experts p1 and p2 (each rates every artifact): balanced artifacts x 2 raters ANOVA; secondary: artifacts with all three experts x 3
phase_c.judge_g_study: each judge: balanced artifacts x 3 repeat calls ANOVA (repeat index is the facet)
phase_c.judge_forecast: 3-call histogram smoothed with the experiment 02/06 primary floor (1 - 6e) q + e, e = 1e-6
phase_c.baseline_forecast: expert marginal histogram on the historical train split, same floor
external_metrics: MAE and bias of the 3-call mean vs the expert mean (0..5)
ICC(A,1) and ICC(C,1) between the judge 3-call mean and the expert mean
phase_c.ranking_comparison: Kendall tau-b between the judge order by internal 1-call Erho2 and by test RPS (5 judges; descriptive; p-val=n/a); paired task-bootstrap differences between the most repeatable judge and the lowest-RPS judge
phase_c.sensitivity: exclude artifacts flagged ref_ambiguous_in_window or ref_placeholder_at_annotation

measurement_contract.expected: mean(q_x) - mean(p_x) = 0 and var(q_x) - var(p_x) = 0 exactly for all 11 artifacts; third raw moment differs by 6 epsilon_x
q_x sums to 1 exactly, q_x > 0, q_x != p_x
exactly (6/5) epsilon_x^2 > 0 per artifact
Brier excess exactly 20 epsilon_x^2; population TVD exactly 4 epsilon_x
KL(p_x || q_x) > 0, finite
Pearson, Spearman and Kendall between forecast means and true means tie exactly (both 1)
population v_u, v_a, v_e, Erho2 and Phi identical for p- and q-panels (exact Fractions)
same exact moment equalities; RPS excess larger than A1 for every artifact (prediction, not a theorem)
95% intervals of the paired mean difference of each raw ANOVA component estimate cover 0 (estimators are unbiased); no directional prediction for SD ratios or coefficient means
deterministic wrong judge: v_e = 0, Erho2 = Phi = 1 exactly, equal to the deterministic oracle; RPS excess and TVD > 0 on j in {9,10,11} and 0 elsewhere; MAE > 0
constant deterministic judge: coefficients undefined; constant sampled judge: coefficients 0

human and shifted-judge panels have identical components and coefficients; bias exactly +1; RPS excess > 0; CE infinite; smoothed CE finite and above the oracle CE; pooled panel keeps Erho2 and lowers Phi
T = 1 has the lowest mean expected RPS and CE in the tempered family; its expected RPS is positive (irreducible disagreement); the mode point mass has infinite CE
sampled-score Erho2 increases as T decreases (prediction); mode point mass gives Erho2 = 1
oracle expected RPS 3/40 in both shift populations, MAE 0; sampled 1-rating Erho2 = 1/3 (narrow) and 5/7 (wide)
single-rating marginal variance 3 and v_u = 1 in both configs; at budget 16 C1 prefers [8,2] and C2 prefers [2,8] for both targets
all 36 formula checks within 3.5 Monte Carlo standard errors

REML selector picks the oracle design at budget 16 (absolute target) in at least 90% of replications in both configs; mean paired observed absolute-error reduction vs the equal design positive with a 95% interval above 0
observed error above the naive prediction and consistent with the (1 + rho) analytic value
pooled prediction near the group average; group H observed error about 0.1 above group L
S1: absolute error unchanged but realized Phi far below the calibration prediction; S2: the calibration-chosen design is no longer the best under the shifted components
calibration-estimated Phi exceeds the realized deployment Phi (inflation by dependent occasions)
judges' 1-call test-retest Erho2 exceeds the 2-expert inter-rater single-rating Erho2 (prediction); no predicted relation between the judge order by reliability and by RPS
